speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin, can you describe the rash on your skin? Is it itchy, painful, or does it resemble bruises?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the recent camping trip and sexually active status are significant clues. Has the rash appeared anywhere on your body besides your skin, and do you have any joint swelling other than the wrist or knee? Also, have you noticed any difficulty moving the wrist joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erysipelas (specifically of the wrist/hand).

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists.

I suspect this is an acute bacterial infection given the fever, chills, and the distinct "proud flesh" appearance of the lesions; can you confirm if you have any known contact with farm animals or recent insect bites?
